He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]]. ==High school career== Etienne began playing high school basketball as a freshman at [[Dwight-Englewood School]] in [[Englewood, New Jersey]]. For his junior season, he transferred to [[Long Island Lutheran Middle and High School]] in [[Brookville, New York]]. As a junior, Etienne averaged 16.5 points and 3.4 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Tyson's Journey: A Jersey Guard Makes A Move To Long Island Powerhouse |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/07/05/tysons-journey-a-jersey-guard-makes-a-move-to-long-island-powerhouse/ |website=Dave's Joint |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=July 5, 2018}} He competed alongside [[Cole Anthony]] with the PSA Cardinals [[Amateur Athletic Union]] program.{{cite web |last1=Sunner |first1=Marshall |title=Through fire and flames: Tyson Etienne's winding journey has him poised to be a breakout star |url=https://thesunflower.com/46494/sports/through-fire-and-flames-tyson-etiennes-winding-journey-has-him-poised-to-be-a-breakout-star/ |website=The Sunflower |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=October 28, 2019}} He played for Putnam Science Academy in [[Putnam, Connecticut]] for a [[postgraduate year]], helping his team reach the National Prep Championship semifinals.{{cite web |title=Tyson Etienne - Men's Basketball |url=https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyson-etienne/5698 |website=Wichita State Athletics |access-date=January 11, 2021}} After high school, Etienne worked with NBA trainer Chris Brickley and trained with several NBA players.{{cite web |last1=Tan |first1=John |title=NBA: Future Prospect Learns From CJ McCollum, Carmelo Anthony And JR Smith |url=https://www.ibtimes.com/nba-future-prospect-learns-cj-mccollum-carmelo-anthony-jr-smith-2859143 |website=[[International Business Times]] |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=November 3, 2019}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] over offers from [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]].{{cite web |last1=Eldridge |first1=Taylor |title=WSU lands second-highest rated recruit in Gregg Marshall era with 2019 four-star guard |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article219693830.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=October 13, 2018}} ==College career== On November 16, 2019, Etienne scored a freshman season-high 21 points, shooting 5-of-8 from three-point range, in a 103–62 win over [[UT Martin Skyhawks men's basketball|UT Martin]].{{cite web |title=Shockers Surge Past Skyhawks |url=https://goshockers.com/news/2019/11/16/mens-basketball-shockers-surge-past-skyhawks.aspx |website=Wichita State Athletics |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=November 16, 2019}} As a freshman, he averaged 9.4 points and shot 38.8 percent from the three-point line. In the offseason, Etienne improved his athleticism and strength.{{cite web |last1=Eldridge |first1=Taylor |title=Breaking down WSU's breakout star: Trainer takes you inside the game of Tyson Etienne |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article248277285.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=January 5, 2021}} On January 2, 2021, he scored 29 points in an 83–79 win over [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].{{cite web |last1=Lilly |first1=Chris |title=Tyson Etienne is having a special start to sophomore season |url=https://www.kake.com/story/43121490/tyson-etienne-is-having-a-special-start-to-sophomore-season |website=[[KAKE (TV)]] |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=January 3, 2021}} As a sophomore, Etienne averaged 16.3 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 1.0 steals per game, earning [[American Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|AAC co-Player of the Year]] honors. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], but ultimately returned to Wichita State.{{cite news |last1=Eldridge |first1=Taylor |title=He's coming back: Tyson Etienne exits NBA Draft to return to Wichita State basketball |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article252630903.html |access-date=September 2, 2021 |work=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |date=July 7, 2021}} In his junior season, Etienne averaged 14.9 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 1.1 steals per game, earning a selection to the Third Team All-AAC.{{cite press release|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/3/8/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men's Basketball Honors|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]] |date=March 9, 2022 |accessdate=March 9, 2022}} On April 21, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while foregoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Marty|first1=Sean |title=Tyson Etienne turns pro and declares for 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://thesunflower.com/62862/sports/tyson-etienne-turns-pro-and-declares-for-2022-nba-draft/|website=The Sunflower |access-date=June 1, 2022 |date=April 21, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===College Park Skyhawks (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Etienne signed with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] on October 22, 2022.{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Finalize Training Camp Schedule and Roster|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-finalize-training-camp-schedule-and-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2022|access-date=September 6, 2024}} ===Brooklyn Nets / Long Island Nets (2024–2026)=== On September 10, 2024, Etienne signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]], but was waived the next day.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Nets Sign, Waive Tyson Etienne|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/nets-to-sign-tyson-etienne.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 11, 2024}} On October 27, he joined the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} After consistently strong performances all season for their G-League affiliate, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and Etienne agreed on a two-way contract on March 4, 2025.{{Cite web|title=Nets sign Tyson Etienne to a two-way deal, waive Kendall Brown|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/03/05/nets-sign-tyson-etienne-to-a-two-way-deal-waive-kendall-brown/|access-date=March 5, 2025|website=nydailynews.com|language=en}} He made his NBA debut on March 28, recording eight points and one assist in a 132–100 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Brian |title=Nets give two prospects a 'dream come true' chance in uncompetitive loss to Clippers |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/nets-two-prospects-dream-come-023720086.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=January 13, 2026 |date=March 28, 2025}} In seven appearances for Brooklyn, Etienne averaged 7.9 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 1.7 assists. On July 3, 2025, Etienne re-signed with the Nets on a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web | title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Tyson Etienne To Two-Way Contract | website=The NBA G League | date=2025-07-03 | url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-tyson-etienne-to-two-way-contract | access-date=2025-12-06}} === Paris Basketball (2026–present) === On July 16, 2026, Etienne signed with played college basketball for [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].{{cite web |last1=Lomonico |first1=Dave |title=PG Etienne Has High-Major Looks, Terps Connections |url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/Article/PG-Etienne-Has-High-Major-Looks-Terps-Connections-118223254/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 11, 2021 |date=May 14, 2018}} His mother, Anita Gibson, is an [[Emmy Award|Emmy]]-nominated [[make-up artist]]. Etienne is a nephew of former NBA player [[Marcus Camby]] and actor [[Omari Hardwick]]. He is a cousin of NBA player [[DeAndre Jordan]] who currently plays for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].
